In proposing these regulations, Staff has attempted to balance
the limited, conditional right that our community has to utilize
public streets for parking against the need to protect the public
health, safety, and welfare from adverse impacts resulting from
the parking of Oversized Vehicles and Unattached Trailers on
public streets.
1. Ordinance focuses on improving health, safety & welfare:
• Safety concerns resulting from diminished visibility
• Insufficient parking for most members of community as a result
of the few that have Oversized Vehicles or unattached trailers
2. Ordinance does NOT completely ban parking of Oversized Vehicles
(as done by other jurisdictions):
• MAY be parked in Non-Residential Districts: 5am to 10pm
• RV Parking Permit Program
• 10 Short-Term/2 Long-Term
• Online applications (easier for owners, reduced cost, and
less staff time)
3. Trailers may still be parked in street if:
• Attached to a motor vehicle; OR,
• Pursuant to a Public Works permit
